ratings.reviewer_notes: Directly reviews cytokine-barrier pathways in AD, including IL-4, IL-13, and IL-22 suppression of filaggrin and keratinocyte alarmin amplification of type 2 inflammation.
Direct human biopsy and keratinocyte evidence that AD-associated IL-4 and IL-13 reduce filaggrin expression, connecting atopic inflammation to barrier defects.
IL-4Rα blockade in AD patients increased filaggrin, loricrin, claudin, and lipid-metabolism genes while suppressing type 2 inflammation, supporting an IL-4/IL-13-mediated barrier pathway.
Specifically describes IL-13-driven barrier dysfunction through downregulation of the OVOL1-filaggrin axis and upregulation of the periostin-IL-24 axis.
Establishes FLG null variants as strong determinants of early-onset, persistent AD, supporting a genetic epidermal-barrier pathway in disease susceptibility.
Directly tests the IL-13–STAT6–periostin–IL-24–STAT3 pathway leading to filaggrin downregulation and barrier dysfunction, with keratinocyte, mouse, and human AD evidence.
Shows that IL-4/IL-13–STAT6 signaling suppresses ELOVL3/ELOVL6 and shifts ceramides and other lipids toward shorter chains, identifying a type 2 cytokine–lipid barrier pathway.

A DNCB mouse intervention study links reduced type 2 cytokines with restored filaggrin and lower transepidermal water loss, but does not isolate the causal pathway connecting AD to barrier dysfunction.
Directly reviews the reciprocal barrier-immune pathway: IL-4/IL-13 suppress filaggrin, while barrier-disrupted keratinocytes release TSLP, IL-25, and IL-33 to promote type 2 inflammation.
Reviews epigenetic mechanisms affecting filaggrin, antimicrobial defenses, microbiome-related dysfunction, and cytokines such as IL-4, IL-13, IL-17, and IL-22 in AD.
Focused review of competing AHR barrier-enhancing and IL-4/IL-13–JAK–STAT6/STAT3 barrier-suppressing axes, including oxidative stress and therapeutic implications.
Describes an IL-33/IL-31 axis linking damaged keratinocytes, Th2 cytokine induction, impaired keratinocyte differentiation, pruritus, scratching, and further barrier disruption.
AD lesion transcriptomics identifies coordinated IL-4/IL-13 signaling, inflammation, keratinization and cornified-envelope pathways, with downregulation of barrier genes including FLG2 and CGNL1.
Directly reviews AD barrier dysfunction and its contributing pathways, including immune dysregulation, FLG mutations, antimicrobial-peptide deficiency, and skin dysbiosis.
Human skin-on-chip model directly shows IL-4/IL-13 signaling through IL-4Rα induces AD-like morphology and reduces filaggrin, loricrin, and involucrin.
Systematic review of barrier restoration by IL-4/IL-13 and JAK inhibition, covering transepidermal water loss, hydration, epidermal thickness, ceramides, and filaggrin.
Directly reviews interactions among barrier component loss, Th2 and keratinocyte cytokines, and itch-scratch signaling as a positive feedback loop maintaining AD.
Provides adjacent model-selection context by identifying barrier defects, reduced filaggrin, cytokines, and neuroinflammation as required AD-model features, but does not primarily delineate pathways.
Direct genetic evidence that loss-of-function variants in the epidermal barrier protein filaggrin strongly predispose to AD, supporting a primary epithelial-barrier route.
Direct ex vivo human-skin evidence that IL-4, IL-13, and IL-22 disrupt barrier integrity and reduce filaggrin and claudin-1, with distinct effects on antimicrobial and receptor pathways.
Generic macrophage, basophil, and immortalized keratinocyte experiments show effects on inflammatory signaling and barrier molecules, but no AD tissue or disease model directly tests the connection.
Mechanistically reviews suppression of filaggrin, loricrin, and involucrin by IL-4, IL-13, IL-17A, and IL-22 through STAT pathways, contrasted with AHR/NRF2-mediated barrier enhancement.
